problem: Existing open-vocabulary 3D maps (VLMaps, CLIP-Fields, NLMap, ConceptFusion) rely almost only on visual-language features and ignore audio, so robots cannot use sound or image cues to disambiguate goals such as 'the table where you heard coughing' when several similar objects exist.
motivation: Humans integrate multiple senses into spatial maps, and sound is a complementary cue for locating and disambiguating goals. Robots lack a unified spatial representation that anchors audio, vision and language together and supports cross-modal reasoning without fine-tuning.
key_idea: Build a unified 3D voxel/topological map that stores visual localization features, pixel-aligned visual-language features, CLIP area features and audio-language features, convert each modality's query into a heatmap, fuse the heatmaps by element-wise multiplication, and drive it from LLM-generated code.
insight: Multiplying heatmaps from different modalities (a sharp primary one and a broad auxiliary one) resolves ambiguity that a single modality cannot. In object-sound indexing, VLMaps+AudioCLIP reaches 53.78% Recall@1 at <0.5m, against 26.05% for AudioCLIP alone. Visual localization lifts visual-object recall from 7.55% to 62.26%. Better audio-language models help (AudioCLIP is much better than wav2clip), and the CLIP sparse map complements the fine-tuned VLMaps features for area concepts. Failures come from compounding errors in the individual modules.
method: Visual Localization Module: NetVLAD global retrieval, SuperPoint/SuperGlue matching and PnP against stored RGB-D frames with odometry give the global pose of a query image.
Object Localization Module: VLMaps-style LSeg/OpenSeg pixel features back-projected into the 3D map; cosine similarity with a text embedding gives the target points.

Area Localization Module: a sparse topological map of CLIP image features tied to poses; text-image similarity gives scored locations for regions like 'kitchen', avoiding the forgetting of fine-tuned segmenters.
Audio Localization Module: silence-detection segmentation of the audio, AudioCLIP/wav2clip/CLAP features per segment stored with odometry; text-to-audio matching gives the location.
Cross-modal heatmap reasoning: each module outputs a 3D heatmap with linear distance decay (primary decay 0.1, auxiliary 0.01); heatmaps are fused by element-wise product and the argmax is the goal.

LLM code generation: an LLM writes Python calling get_major_map / get_map (obj, sound, img), load_image, get_max_pos_3d and move_to for multimodal and spatial goals; a ROS navigation stack is used for planning on the real robot.

setting.backbone: Frozen pretrained models: LSeg/OpenSeg, CLIP, AudioCLIP (also wav2clip/CLAP), NetVLAD, SuperPoint, SuperGlue, plus an LLM for code generation (LLM not named in the text)
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot; uses off-the-shelf pretrained foundation models)
setting.observation: RGB-D video with audio track and odometry, used to build the map offline
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward 0.1 m, turn left 5°, turn right 5°, stop (simulation); ROS global/local planner on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat with Matterport3D (10 scenes, ESC-50 audio); real Ridgeback + Panda robot
setting.privileged: Map built beforehand from a manually collected exploration video with odometry (pre-exploration); sound sources are artificially inserted at known positions; ground-truth region map only in one oracle ablation

numbers_note: Only self-collected benchmarks, no standard ones. Real-world results are in text: 50% overall success on 20 multimodal tasks, 6/10 on multimodal spatial goals.
results: AVLMaps reaches 77.5% independent subgoal success on sound navigation and 46.2% on ambiguous sound goals, versus 22.0% for the VLMaps+wav2clip multimodal baseline. Object-sound Recall@1 at <0.5m is 53.78% vs 26.05% for AudioCLIP alone, and visual-object recall is 62.26% vs 7.55% without visual localization. Real-robot success is 50% on 20 tasks and 6/10 on spatial goals.
limitations: Sensitive to audio noise, and assumes a static environment during mapping and use
Failures compound across modules (rare objects, confusing sounds), and area localization stays weak (Recall@1 35.56% at <2m)
Evaluated on small self-built benchmarks with artificially inserted audio, and real-world tests are small and offline-mapped
